# Test review rules

**Primary focus: determinism.** Same controlled inputs must verify the same contract, independent of test order, parallel activity, host state, and incidental timing.

## Review sequence

1. Read changed tests, setup/cleanup, and the exercised production path. Identify the contract and uncontrolled dependencies.
2. Check input control, state isolation, synchronization, then assertions and supported feature/platform/release configurations.
3. Test the smallest unit that owns the contract; mock its collaborators. Use pipeline tests only for integration contracts. For concurrency, verify invariants across explored schedules, not one fixed schedule.
4. Report only evidenced defects: cite the source, name the wrong outcome or uncontrolled dependency, and recommend the smallest coverage-preserving fix. Use existing seams and repository policy; skip style nits and unrelated legacy cleanup.

Passing CI, snapshots, stress reruns, or a closed bug do not prove determinism or a root-cause fix. Distinguish harness defects from product races; preserve security checks and meaningful assertions.

## Rules

Use the applicable recommendation, not a fixed number of solutions.
Markers are search hints, not proof of a defect; check usage and imported aliases.

| Avoid | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| Substring assertions instead of checking the result. Markers: `assert!(x.contains(...))`, `.contains(`. | Prefer full `insta` snapshots or exact string/structured equality. Control inputs; normalize only incidental values. Use `starts_with` for prefix contracts, checking any meaningful remainder. Use `contains` only when containment itself is the contract. |
| Negative tests that accept any error or generic error text. Markers: `.is_err()`, `.unwrap_err().to_string()`. | Assert typed causes and fields after successful setup reaches the intended branch. Test exact error wording separately with deterministic inputs. |
| Checking only that output is nonempty or an operation failed. Markers: `assert!(!x.is_empty())`, `.success()`, `.failure()`. | Assert the expected values, state changes, and side effects. Distinguish relevant outcomes; add a contrasting case when needed. |
| Requiring a full pipeline for a utility test, or mocking the behavior being asserted. | Call the utility directly with deterministic mocked collaborators. Reports, probes, and policies can be mocked when they are dependencies, not the subject of the assertion. Use wider integration tests only to verify wiring or cross-component contracts. |
| Network services, tool installation, sign-in, browsers, or developer credentials in unit tests. Markers: `reqwest::`, `TcpStream::connect`, `Command::new`. | Mock service and host dependencies. Put real integration in separately provisioned jobs. |
| Unspecified collaborators silently succeeding or reaching the host. | Reject unexpected calls; script only scenario-required interactions. |
| Shared mutable fixtures, caches, or target directories. | Own mutable state and temporary directories per test; share only immutable inputs. |
| Global counters, hooks, or registries isolated only by atomics, save/restore, or partial locks. Markers: `static`, `AtomicUsize`, `set_hook`, `take_hook`, `thread_local!`. | Prefer owned state. Thread-local state works only if all observed work stays on that thread. Isolate unavoidable global scenarios in dedicated test-harness executables. |
| Tracing assertions/coverage depending on first callsite registration. Markers: `set_global_default`, `set_default`, `rebuild_interest_cache`. | Initialize a compatible subscriber that keeps tested callsites interested before use; attribute captured events per test, including cross-thread work. Isolate no-subscriber cases. Cache reset afterward does not prevent concurrent interference. |
| Process environment/cwd mutation or host-dependent fixture paths. Markers: `set_var`, `remove_var`, `set_current_dir`, `current_dir`. | Pass explicit environment and working-directory inputs; resolve fixture paths from a test-owned base. |
| Wall-clock/random assertions or sleeps for ordering. Markers: `SystemTime::now`, `Instant::now`, `Utc::now`, `thread_rng`, `rand::rng`, `sleep`, `sleep_until`. | Inject clocks and seeded/scripted randomness; synchronize with channels, barriers, notifications, or an injected scheduler. |
| Permission changes, lock races, or mandatory privileges to provoke I/O errors. Markers: `set_permissions`, `chmod`, `symlink`. | Inject the failing syscall. For real OS tests, provision/check capabilities; report only recognized unsupported-condition skips and fail other setup errors. |
| Security fixtures under uncontrolled checkout ancestry or relaxed production permission checks. | Verify test-owned directory ownership and ancestry. Inject metadata for policy tests; exercise OS enforcement separately. A temp directory alone proves no security property. |
| Public CA lifecycle, machine trust stores, or online issuer retrieval in ordinary certificate tests. | Supply a complete test chain, explicit root, fixed time, and disabled network retrieval; or inject the chain engine and provision OS integration separately. Keep hostname/wrong-root/policy rejection coverage. Test-only trust hooks must be narrowly gated and fail closed. |
| Protocol mismatches hidden by transport retries. | Configure matching client/server protocols and negotiation; establish the handshake before benchmarking. |
| Generated fake executables for canned tool results. Markers: `fs::write`, `Command::new`, `.sh`, `.bat`, `ETXTBSY`. | Inject a runner returning status/stdout/stderr to real parsing code. For process compatibility, use a provisioned real tool or immutable prebuilt helper separately. |
| Test helpers in default APIs or mismatched feature/backend gates. Markers: `#[cfg(`, `[features]`, `default =`, `required-features`. | Keep private tests in their crate; gate exported helpers behind a non-default test-support feature, not workspace defaults. Align cfg/imports/bench `required-features`; check production consumers without test features and supported partial-feature combinations. |
| Machine-speed assertions or undifferentiated unit/integration/instrumented budgets. Markers: `.elapsed()`, `Duration::from_`, `timeout`. | Investigate measured outliers against repository budgets, excluding compilation. Separate groups with concurrency/deadlines. Use work bounds or benchmarks for performance; deadlines are safety limits, not speed assertions. |
| External-process jobs without bounded waits, diagnostics, and cleanup. Markers: `.spawn()`, `.wait()`, `.wait_with_output()`. | Capture diagnostics; terminate and reap process trees on timeout. Prefer in-process collaborators when process compatibility is irrelevant. |
| Unbounded concurrency models or ignored models as a permanent timeout fix. Markers: `loom::model`, `loom::model::Builder`, `#[ignore]`. | Reduce to the synchronization invariant; justify exploration bounds and state excluded schedules. Keep bounded models in ordinary gates and deeper exploration in deadline-bound jobs. |
| Blanket Miri exclusions for one unsupported dependency. Markers: `cfg(not(miri))`, `cfg_attr(miri, ignore`. | Ignore only affected tests with reasons; keep unaffected tests enabled. |
| Exact allocation counts for operations the optimizer may elide. | Assert observable allocator contracts in relevant release profiles. For telemetry, use explicit allocator operations and opaque inputs; `black_box` is not an allocation guarantee. |
| Source-loop assumptions about stable machine callsites or stack layout. Markers: `Backtrace`, `#[inline`, `black_box`. | Assert aggregate invariants unless grouping is the contract. For grouping, control callsites with non-inlined helpers and opaque inputs in optimized profiles. Elision and callsite duplication need different fixes. |
| Misleading benchmark timing/memory claims or oversized stack fixtures. | Exclude setup/teardown/counting from timing; include the claimed algorithm work. Label truncation/bounds and counting exclusions; measure peak RAM to claim it. Construct large fixtures directly on the heap or use bounded/iterative setup. Keep expensive sweeps out of ordinary tests with explicit `--bench` selection and appropriate `test = false`/`harness = false`. |
| Retries, longer sleeps, weaker assertions, ignored tests, or nonrecurrence presented as fixes. Markers: `retry`, `sleep`, `#[ignore]`. | Remove the evidenced uncontrolled dependency while preserving coverage. Keep unresolved product races under investigation. Temporary quarantine must name lost coverage, owner, and restoration condition. |
